description: IDENTITY: ServiceAccount northstar:agent-readonly exists on the cluster — the agent operates as a real identity, not the admin kubeconfig
command: kubectl get sa agent-readonly -n northstar -o jsonpath='{.metadata.name}' 2>/dev/null || echo missing

description: IDENTITY: the read-only kubeconfig CAN get pods — the identity is not so locked down it cannot do its job
command: KC=platform/kubeconfigs/agent-readonly.yaml; [ -f "$KC" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; kubectl --kubeconfig="$KC" auth can-i get pods -n northstar 2>/dev/null || echo no

description: IDENTITY: the read-only kubeconfig cannot delete a Deployment — the API server refuses it, not a hook
command: KC=platform/kubeconfigs/agent-readonly.yaml; [ -f "$KC" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; OUT=$(kubectl --kubeconfig="$KC" auth can-i delete deployments -n northstar 2>/dev/null); echo "${OUT:-no}"

description: IDENTITY: generated agent kubeconfigs are gitignored — the token that grants cluster access is never checked into Git
command: git check-ignore -q platform/kubeconfigs/agent-readonly.yaml && echo ignored || echo tracked

description: IDENTITY: the remediator CAN patch Deployments in the northstar namespace — the identity exists to do the one job it is scoped for
command: KC=platform/kubeconfigs/agent-remediator.yaml; [ -f "$KC" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; kubectl --kubeconfig="$KC" auth can-i patch deployments -n northstar 2>/dev/null || echo no

description: IDENTITY: the remediator CANNOT patch Deployments in kube-system — a namespaced Role, not a ClusterRole, so the write scope stops at the namespace boundary
command: KC=platform/kubeconfigs/agent-remediator.yaml; [ -f "$KC" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; OUT=$(kubectl --kubeconfig="$KC" auth can-i patch deployments -n kube-system 2>/dev/null); echo "${OUT:-no}"

description: IDENTITY: the remediator cannot delete Deployments — its verbs are get/list/patch only, deletion is a different authority it was never granted
command: KC=platform/kubeconfigs/agent-remediator.yaml; [ -f "$KC" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; OUT=$(kubectl --kubeconfig="$KC" auth can-i delete deployments -n northstar 2>/dev/null); echo "${OUT:-no}"

description: IDENTITY: the remediator cannot read Secrets — it is narrower than the read-only identity, not a superset of it, even though it can write
command: KC=platform/kubeconfigs/agent-remediator.yaml; [ -f "$KC" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; OUT=$(kubectl --kubeconfig="$KC" auth can-i get secrets -n northstar 2>/dev/null); echo "${OUT:-no}"

description: HARNESS: k8s-operator carries the Skill tool — without it k8s-triage is read as a plain file and no schema-bound triage ever fires
command: awk '/^tools:/' .claude/agents/k8s-operator.md 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'Skill' && echo present || echo missing

description: TOOL: kubectl-bounded refuses -A — an unbounded cluster-wide read is not something a triage agent is allowed to ask for
command: platform/bin/kubectl-bounded get pods -A >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -ne 0 ] && echo refused || echo allowed

description: TOOL: output past MAX_LINES carries the TRUNCATED marker — an unbounded read is a context-budget grenade even when it is legally scoped
command: [ -f platform/kubeconfigs/agent-readonly.yaml ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; MAX_LINES=1 platform/bin/kubectl-bounded get pods -n northstar 2>/dev/null | grep -q -- '--- TRUNCATED:' && echo truncated || echo not-truncated

description: SKILL: k8s-triage/SKILL.md names all six schema fields — five free-form essays cannot be ranked against each other, five identical records can
command: S=.claude/skills/k8s-triage/SKILL.md; [ -f "$S" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; for f in workload signature root_cause evidence blast_radius confidence; do grep -q "$f" "$S" || { echo incomplete; exit 0; }; done; echo complete

description: SKILL: the evidence commands read .conditions.ready on EndpointSlices, and no bounded read is a bare 'kubectl get endpoints' — the ADDRESSES column lies about which pods are actually serving
command: S=.claude/skills/k8s-triage/SKILL.md; [ -f "$S" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -q 'conditions.ready' "$S" || { echo wrong; exit 0; }; awk '/^```bash/{c=1;next} /^```/{c=0} c && /get endpoints /{bad=1} END{exit !bad}' "$S" && echo wrong || echo correct

description: ENFORCEMENT: the deny hook returns a deny decision for a mutating kubectl verb — a faster, louder no in front of the RBAC 403
command: echo '{"tool_input":{"command":"kubectl delete pod foo -n northstar"}}' | .claude/hooks/deny-cluster-mutation.sh 2>/dev/null | grep -q '"decision":"deny"' && echo deny || echo allow

description: YOUR BRIEF: the directory's standing context (platform/CLAUDE.md) carries no 'done means' requirements text — a CLAUDE.md is injected every turn forever, a one-time brief is not
command: [ -f platform/CLAUDE.md ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -qi 'done means' platform/CLAUDE.md && echo leaked || echo separate

description: YOUR BRIEF: platform/SPEC.md exists and states what done means — the triage requirements are written down before the agent starts
command: S=platform/SPEC.md; [ -f "$S" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -qi 'done means' "$S" && echo authored || echo incomplete

description: YOUR FINDINGS: agentops/k8s-triage/findings.md names all five planted workloads — imagepull, crashloop, resource-limit, liveness-probe and configmap-mount
command: F=agentops/k8s-triage/findings.md; [ -f "$F" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; ok=1; for w in imagepull-test crashloop-test resource-limit-test liveness-probe-test configmap-mount-test; do grep -q "$w" "$F" || ok=0; done; [ "$ok" = 1 ] && echo covers-all-five || echo incomplete

description: YOUR FINDINGS: all five findings carry a blast_radius field and the file states a ranking by blast radius — five identical records are useless unless they are ordered
command: F=agentops/k8s-triage/findings.md; [ -f "$F" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; n=$(grep -c 'blast_radius:' "$F" 2>/dev/null || echo 0); grep -qi 'rank' "$F" && [ "$n" -ge 5 ] && echo ranked || echo unranked

description: YOUR REMEDIATION: agentops/k8s-triage/remediation.md records the fix as applied through the agent-remediator identity, not the admin kubeconfig
command: F=agentops/k8s-triage/remediation.md; [ -f "$F" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -q 'agent-remediator' "$F" && ! grep -qi 'kubeconfigs/admin.yaml' "$F" && echo remediator-identity || echo wrong-identity

description: YOUR MEASUREMENT: agentops/k8s-triage/secret-read-measurement.md records whether 'get secret -o yaml' succeeded under the read-only identity — the honest-limits beat has to be measured, not assumed
command: F=agentops/k8s-triage/secret-read-measurement.md; [ -f "$F" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -qiE 'succeeded|failed|forbidden|allowed|denied' "$F" && echo measured || echo unmeasured
